title: I made an automated 24/7 game dev system. How to handle collaboration for open-source
author: uskyeeeee
selftext:
I built a system that can develop games 24/7.

I’d love to open-source it, but I’m still figuring out how multiple developers can collaborate on such a fully automated system.

comments.author: Accomplished-Gap2989
comments.body: Why do you need anyone if it's fully automated? Shouldn't it just produce games on its own?

replies.author: uskyeeeee
replies.body: Because I don’t have enough tokens.

replies.author: Saxxiefone
replies.body: Bro invented an "infinite source of energy" that needs fuel

comments.author: Trashy_io
comments.body:
I don't think this is something people are asking for tbh, I don't think creative processes should be completely automated just the un-creative parts. 

I could be wrong but this is the type of stuff devs and gamers are actually super against in terms of AI use. 

For example what value is it providing? There is over 300k+ indie devs or people wanting to become indie devs. That are going to produce way better results then an automated 24/7 system because art isn't just a calculation of whats next but how it makes a person feel. Behind every great game is a ton of intent and creative expression which makes the game have a feeling. That feeling is a connection between the artist and the viewer. 

This is coming from someone who a advocate for AI and uses it themselves. I hope this opens up some realizations for you as far as what the current thoughts of the general public is and why. If I were you Id try to plan on how to rebuild it so it's a creative tool not a replacement.

replies.author: uskyeeeee
replies.body: But someone has to build it first to prove that 24‑hour automated games lack creativity and can’t compete with indie devs, right?

replies.author: Trashy_io
replies.body:
eh, I don't think its worth the time investment personally, especially at this point in time. But if you must be the one to do so best of luck but there are many platforms that already do this just not 24/7. I just don't see how you will gain anything  from the project as it sits. It is clear at the moment purely generated games do not sell or gain any traction because they lack a lot of polish and content where indie games that's their sweet spot.  Going to be pretty hard to have AI design and create a unique and interesting main menu or cohesive storyline. These are things AI will be generic and requires human creativity.

You have any projects to link? Id like to see the quality of the automated process and how it differs from title to title

replies.author: schmurfy2
replies.body:
Ai has its use as a tool but fully automating it seems to be the new hot trend and I just don't get it....    
You spend a lot of feal money so that an atonomous system will produce hot garbage, to do what ? I highly doubt you will get something you can sell at the end of the process, of there is even an end.

The issue isn't even with the lack of human interaction or creativity but what os the end goal ? Flooding the net with garbage like we already have on mobile ? Why not learn to code instead and really build something?(You can even use AI to help you)

replies.author: harmonicrain
replies.body:
The thing is some of us arent spending mad money - I'm using the google cloud 200 dollars free credit for gemini - wouldnt have had a use case otherwise as google cloud sucks balls.

Claude Pro is only 20 a month, between using that, gemini and opencode, i have everything covered for barely anything. 

Heck if you use openrouter, id argue Step 3.5 flash is better than Gemini 3 Flash, and it's free.

replies.author: tconn85
replies.body: You might be surprised by the amount of gamers who just want to play a good game and have zero interest in how it was made. Not that this system will produce good games but eventually if it puts enough shots up something might hit.

replies.author: schmurfy2
replies.body:
You said it though, you need a good game and I would be a bit harder than you by saying that it will definitely not come from an automated system....   
Building a game might not be hard but building a good game is a whole other story.

replies.author: uskyeeeee
replies.body: It’s a simple idea: if a game AI can play a game and play it well, then it can also build it on its own—without any human intervention.

replies.author: Newbietoallofthis
replies.body: So a human doesn't even yell it what kind of game to make?

comments.author: AwesomeWz
comments.body: I have endless tokens. If you can convince me your system worth it.

comments.author: poponis
comments.body:
Why?
This is one example of what I describe as "nobody asked for this".

comments.author: AgenticGameDev
comments.body: As some one who is on 2x20x max plan... Tokens are not the problem of AI today. It might work for simpler stuff but as soon as complexity increase the AI start to fault. Handholding is very important. AI amplify us not replace us. For sure you can make a 24x7 AI today that spits out packman and such. But if you want more complex not so much. Sure I'm on the far end of that doing multiplayer VR for B2B. That is not something a single system can just figure out. No matter how much loops it get it will convert to a error loop where it will fail. AI lack still conceptual understanding.

replies.author: uskyeeeee
replies.body:
I’m on the OpenAI Pro plan. It uses up 20% of my quota just running for 24 hours, and I also need it for work, so I do have a bit of token anxiety.

VR is complicated, that’s true. But the core reason AI can’t do it isn’t complexity—it’s that AI can’t play the games it makes. So the self-looping condition can’t be achieved.

replies.author: AgenticGameDev
replies.body: Yes it can if you do proper E2E test… it’s super hard to make but if you design it right AI can…

replies.author: AgenticGameDev
replies.body: I totally understand ai tokens burn fast.
